name: F01_foundation
title: The biological sampling unit is the polygon, not the pixel
how: Counts use distinct GlobalIDs. A repeated ID can occur in two acquisition-year cells. Audit FAIL refers to a tested claim failing, not a concealed pipeline error.
learn: The library has broad category coverage but only four site/year cells. The experimental independence and truth limits are explicit.
uncertain: Polygon purity, absolute reflectance units and independent annual/field fraction truth are not verified. Distinct nearby polygons can remain spatially correlated.

name: F02_separability
title: Different spectra: effect size, statistical evidence and sensor retention
how: Each heatmap row is one of ten category pairs. All four cohorts remain visible. Ratios measure standardized effect retention, not prediction accuracy or a probability.
learn: All ten whole-spectrum contrasts are supported in the four observed cohorts after declared blocked permutation correction. Effect magnitude and OLI retention vary by pair/domain.
uncertain: Absolute physical units remain unresolved. Convolution can smooth within-class variability, so a standardized effect ratio above one is possible. Synthetic OLI is not independent Landsat evidence.

name: F03_wavelength_separability
title: Wavelength-level differences retain their domain context
how: Top: signed matched effect, class A minus B in the displayed pair. Bottom: adjusted evidence; 1.30 corresponds to p=.05. Grey intervals are masked gaps. Color limits bound display only.
learn: Many broad regions are supported, but sign/magnitude/rank stability is pair- and domain-dependent. All coordinates share whole-curve permutation shuffles; adjacent channels are not independent tests.
uncertain: The lower map is evidence against exchangeability, not an effect confidence interval. Full-cohort maps are descriptive and never used to select predictive features. Null standard errors and every unbounded effect are saved.

name: F04_single_coordinate_recognition
title: Statistical differences do not guarantee individual recognition
how: Left is a five-class problem (chance BA=.20); shaded ranges are observed outer-fold ranges. Right contains ten separate binary problems (chance=.50). No coordinate is chosen using these test scores.
learn: Single-coordinate five-class recognition is limited. Herbaceous versus Woody shrub remains especially weak under the fixed pairwise rule despite supported differences.
uncertain: This tests specified mean-based rules, not all possible nonlinear classifiers. Observed maxima are descriptive and not validated operational bands.

name: F05_complementarity_controls
title: Complementary selection adds value, but random bands can catch up
how: Selected and random subsets use identical inner folds and tuning grids. Five fixed random paths are averaged; shaded envelopes include seed/fold variation, not confidence intervals. PCA uses every input wavelength.
learn: Selected subsets improve modest-budget average recognition. The gap narrows at large budgets; two/three-band held-site controls can favor random subsets. High correlation does not make every additional band useless.
uncertain: No seed or budget is chosen from outer scores. Five random controls do not establish an optimal selector, universal intrinsic dimension or optimized sensor. PCA fit uses annual rows within training only.

name: F06_class_and_domain_failures
title: Recognition failures are class-specific and domain-dependent
how: Recall measures recovered true-category observations. Confusion rows sum to one. Paired-year targets keep the same held identities and trained model; global-year targets change site composition.
learn: Woody shrub transfers poorly relative to Evergreen/background. Controlled paired NEON recognition drops in both temporal directions and is asymmetric. OLI can be less temporally sensitive despite lower familiar-domain recognition.
uncertain: Static retrospective annotations test footprint recognition, not annual biological truth. Three sites and one repeatedly observed site cannot isolate ecological, illumination and processing causes.

name: F07_abundance_controls
title: Synthetic abundance gains depend on domain, priors and retained library
how: All main models see identical outer mixtures. Macro RMSE is sqrt(mean class MSE) within target then averaged across folds. The fairness control reduces ridge to the exact 15 MESMA candidates; the original ridge uses 120 parents.
learn: Ridge120 improves the primary new-parent/held-site benchmark, but fails the global-year prior on average. Ridge15 loses the NEON advantage. Projection improves error. The known-generating-parent oracle has near-zero fraction error.
uncertain: The candidate control changes training diversity/bundle count and model prior; it does not prove a single cause. Methods are not intrinsically ranked, and these algebraic fractions are not field cover.

name: F08_fraction_calibration
title: Zero, low and pure-end mixtures reveal shrinkage hidden by RMSE
how: Each point averages predictions at a nominal truth-grid fraction, first count-weighting machine-precision-equivalent bins within fold, then averaging held sites. The diagonal represents unbiased mean recovery. Endpoints are synthetic pure-parent mixtures, not verified pure materials.
learn: Many methods overpredict absent categories and shrink high fractions. Similar overall RMSE can hide different class-specific biases and detection behavior.
uncertain: Mean calibration curves hide bundle variation; paired intervals and per-fold/per-class errors remain saved. No universal field detection threshold follows from this grid.

name: F09_detection_and_class_links
title: Recognition, false detection and quantification are different outcomes
how: Rows are researcher categories and columns are methods. False detection and low-fraction misses use the declared .10 final-fraction cutoff. The final panel shows empirical detection frequency versus truth, ridge solid and two-stage dashed. Class-level links are saved separately for all five categories.
learn: Harder-to-recognize categories also tend to have larger ridge fraction error here. False detection and missed low fractions trade off; a stronger prior can improve one while worsening the other.
uncertain: Class-level associations are descriptive, not five independent geographic replicates. Stage-A presence metrics are separately saved; .10 is a comparison rule, not an independently validated detection limit.

name: F10_ambiguity_and_limits
title: Better expected fractions do not establish unique physical inversion
how: Ambiguity is maximum candidate-class fraction range among near-fitting solutions at the declared .01 tolerance. High means range >=.30. Every scatter point is one saved synthetic mixture, not an independent plant.
learn: Ridge can reduce error in high-ambiguity targets while alternatives remain feasible. The moderate stratum can favor MESMA. Spectral reconstruction is insufficient, and derivatives do not remedy the main limitations.
uncertain: Candidate/tolerance ambiguity is not exhaustive physical uncertainty. The class burden is mixture-level ambiguity conditional on category presence. Observational data cannot uniquely apportion library variability, overlap, acquisition shift and prior effects.
